description:
Bracket access on a keyword list ABORTS the process on every door.

  opts = [timeout: 30, retries: 2]
  opts[:timeout]

  fz run/interp/build:
    panicked at runtime/src/ir_runtime.rs:1654:
    fz_struct_get_named_field_ref: ExpectedTag { expected: ValueKind(3), found: ValueKind(1) }
    fatal runtime error: failed to initiate panic, error 5, aborting
  Elixir: 30   (and nil for a missing key)

`lhs[key]` is parsed as `Access.get/2` (frontdoor.rs bracket-access rule) and
decoded back into `Expr::Index` (quoted_function.rs is_access_get). `Expr::Index`
assumes a map or struct receiver and reaches a struct field read with a LIST
tag, which is not a diagnostic -- it is a non-unwinding abort.

Elixir's `Access` works on keyword lists as well as maps, and `opts[:key]` over
a keyword list is one of the most common shapes in real Elixir code.

MATTERS FOR THIS EPIC: fz-5xp.13 adds `Keyword`, whose entire surface is
keyword lists, and `keyword()` is already a declared type in runtime.fz. Any
`Keyword` code a user writes will reach for `opts[:key]`.

Pre-existing -- unrelated to fz-5xp.4, which only stopped `Alias.get/2` being
mistaken for an index. Found while writing that ticket's fixture, which
originally covered keyword bracket access and had to be narrowed.

FIX SHAPE: `Expr::Index` needs to dispatch on the receiver -- map/struct as
today, keyword list by key lookup, and anything else a clean diagnostic rather
than a struct read on a mistagged value.

comments.text:
SCOPE CORRECTED after review: this is not about keyword lists. It is the
atom-key `Index` lowering, and keyword lists are one instance.

src/compiler2/jobs/body.rs:1636-1655 lowers `Expr::Index` with an ATOM key to
`ExprStep::FieldAccess` -- struct-field semantics -- and only a non-atom key to
`MapIndex`. So EVERY atom-key bracket access on a non-map/non-struct aborts,
and `nil` is the common case, not an exotic one:

  n = %{outer: %{inner: 7}}
  n[:nope][:x]      elixir nil
                    fz interp: "StructField: subject is not a map or Struct",
                    process aborts
  nil[:a]           elixir nil     fz aborts

  opts = [timeout: 30]
  opts[:timeout]    elixir 30      fz aborts (the case this ticket was filed for)

Conversely `%Struct{}[:field]` SUCCEEDS in fz where Elixir refuses to compile,
because `Access` is not implemented for structs. So the lowering is both too
permissive and too fragile, in the same rule.

FIX SHAPE: `Expr::Index` should dispatch on the RECEIVER, not on the key's kind
-- map by key lookup, keyword list by key lookup, struct refused, anything else
a diagnostic rather than a struct read on a mistagged value. Deciding by key
kind is what makes `nil[:a]` an abort and `%Struct{}[:f]` a success.

Chained access is the shape that makes this urgent: `a[:x][:y]` where `a[:x]`
misses is ordinary Elixir and currently kills the process.

Related: fz-5xp.26 (integer key + atom value panics the compiler),
fz-5xp.27 (tuple/list keys never match), fz-5xp.28 (no Access module).
Together these four are the bracket-access surface, and fz-5xp.12's `Map`
work will meet all of them.

title: Bracket access decides by key kind, not receiver, and aborts on nil/list
